analyzed_vuln.description: SkVertices::Decode deserializes attacker-controlled vertex data and, for attributes with fHasMarkerName set, passes reader.readString() directly into SkVertices::Attribute. Attribute's constructor immediately calls strlen(markerName). The decode path does not enforce that the serialized string is NUL-terminated within the provided byte array, so strlen can run past the end of the allocated SkData buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow read.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger via image filter deserialization path that reaches SkPictureData::create_vertices_from_buffer -> SkVertices::Decode on untrusted bytes (e.g., embedded skp/picture data in SkPictureImageFilter). Input must set attrCount>0 and encodedAttrs[i].fHasMarkerName=true, and provide marker-name bytes without an in-bounds terminating NUL (or otherwise malformed string bounds), so reader.readString() yields a pointer that is consumed as a C-string by strlen in Attribute ctor.
